How to read this globe

Scope. Strict direct-radiocarbon catalogue, ending at 1000 BCE. The expanded catalogue imports directly radiocarbon-dated skeletal individuals from AADR v62.0, with laboratory codes and calibrated intervals, plus the previously verified basket. This is a conservative corrected subset, not a comprehensive worldwide inventory. No dates from other methods or merely associated layers qualify.

Artifact colors. Marker colors follow a fixed logarithmic scale from 1 to 10,000+ reported items. These are source-defined samples: individual objects, lithic debris, fragments, ornaments, or wall images. A panel can be one unit; a hundred fragments need not be a hundred original objects. Lower bounds and approximate values are identified in each count description. Unknown counts are gray, never invented or treated as zero.

Not a population heat map. This is a count-colored point map with halos, not a continuous statistical density surface. Excavation effort, preservation, counting units, and publication history strongly affect the colors. Sites with one highlighted object may contain many other uncounted finds. No grand artifact total is reported because those units are not comparable.

Dates and the slider. The timeline starts at 12,000 BCE and ends at 1000 BCE. Conservative mode shows an entry at its youngest boundary; range-overlap mode shows its oldest possible boundary. These are published age ranges or explicitly approximate summaries, not exact years of manufacture. Markers accumulate and remain visible as time advances. Colors count eligible dated individuals/objects at the selected date, not all finds or population. The coverage reflects sampled research, not a measured explosion of civilization.

Time conventions. Cal BP is calendar years before 1950. A BP age is converted to approximate BCE by subtracting 1950. The numeric slider is not evidence for one-year precision. Radiocarbon years are not calendar years; calibrated published ranges are used when available. Choose linear or logarithmic time.

Carbon-dating rule for ALL entries. The counted objects themselves, or their constituent organic material, must have documented radiocarbon measurements. Site association alone is insufficient. Undated companion objects are excluded. Stone tools dated by surrounding deposits, uranium-series paintings, and geological-age finds have been removed. Radiocarbon age estimates have uncertainty and require calibration; directly dating material does not establish an exact manufacture year.

Locations. Latitude/longitude are approximate site or locality centers, not surveyed findspots; each detail card states its coordinate basis. Coordinates are for orientation, not field navigation. The globe uses modern coastlines—not reconstructed Ice Age shorelines or ancient borders. No present-day territorial claim is implied.

Sources and uncertainty. Expanded skeletal records come from AADR v62.0 (Harvard Dataverse DOI 10.7910/DVN/FFIDCW), downloaded from the gebregl/allen_ancient_dna mirror. Only direct IntCal20/SHCal20 records with a conventional measurement, laboratory code, valid coordinates, and a complete calibrated interval within 12,000–1000 BCE are included. Duplicate person IDs and lab codes are excluded. This is research-sample coverage, not the total archaeological record. Research papers, institutional reports, museums and heritage authorities are preferred. Some entries use clearly linked secondary summaries. Claims described as “oldest” are tied to particular categories and research dates, not timeless rankings. A lack of mapped evidence is not evidence of absence.

Controls. Drag to rotate; wheel, pinch, or +/− to zoom. Arrow keys rotate the focused globe. Click a list entry to center it. Export downloads the entire researched catalogue, not just the currently filtered view. The site catalogue is searchable and sortable.
